title: Investigation Bento-Box: compact observability cookbook
content:
Purpose:
A compact, opinionated "bento-box" of observability panels, metrics definitions, and trace contracts designed to make investigation-first triage fast and consistent for inference incidents. This is intentionally prescriptive — the goal is that oncall can open one small panel set and quickly answer: 1) is this a latency/cost/quality problem, 2) is it tenant-, model-, or infra-scoped, and 3) what immediate mitigations to apply.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: SRE/oncall rotations, observability stewards, and serving-runtime engineers.
- Secondary: product owners who want compact incident narratives, solutions engineers for customer-facing triage.
- Scope: real-time triage for hosted & dedicated pools. Private deployment specifics (airgapped) get annotation notes at the bottom.

Bento-box concept (what it is):
- A single, narrow dashboard pane (~6 micro-panels) per incident type (latency spike, cold-kv tail, increased token-cost, model-hallucination).
- Each pane includes: quick-lens metrics (1–3 numbers), a heatmap/quantile panel, a recent-trace sample list (linkable), tenant-weighted bar, and the top-3 correlated signals.
- Design principle: answer the triage questions within 90s. If deeper analysis needed, the pane links to a more detailed investigation workbook.

Standard metric definitions in this cookbook (canonical names + calc):
1) ttf_first_token_ms (unit: ms)
   - Definition: time from ReceiveTimestamp to first token emitted on stream (median/50, p90, p99).
   - Calculation: first_token_time - request_received_time. Tag: model, route, pool_id, tenant_id, quantization_profile.

2) generation_tail_latency_ms (unit: ms)
   - Definition: time between first_token and last_token for completed responses; use p50/p90/p99 to capture long tails.
   - Calculation: last_token_timestamp - first_token_timestamp. Exclude partial/stream-cancelled responses.

3) kv_cache_hit_rate (unit: pct)
   - Definition: prefix KV cache effective hit rate at serving layer (tenant-scoped and global).
   - Calculation: kv_hits / (kv_hits + kv_misses) over 5m windows. Roll up by tenant and route.

4) continuous_batching_efficiency (unit: tokens/sec-per-GPU)
   - Definition: tokens processed per GPU-second at runtime; helps detect batching regressions.
   - Calculation: tokens_processed / gpu_seconds. Tag: model_variant, sequence_length_bucket.

5) token_cost_ratio (unit: USD/token relative)
   - Definition: approximate per-token cost combining GPU time + amortized model memory premium. Useful when cost alarms trip.
   - Calculation: (gpu_seconds * pool_unit_cost + memory_surcharge) / tokens_generated. (Derived metric, updated by finance ratecard).

6) output_quality_regression_rate (unit: pct)
   - Definition: ratio of eval-set failure / human-review flags over baseline; surfaced by model-quality probes.

Trace contract and span taxonomy (compact conventions for bento-box traces):
- Root span: request.receive (tags: request_id, tenant_id, route, pool_id, model_variant)
- Child spans (shorthand):
  - routing.resolve (tags: fallback_reason, chosen_model_variant)
  - kv.lookup (tags: kv_hit boolean, kv_ttl, tenant_shard)
  - batch.slot (tags: batch_size, sequence_len_bucket)
  - model.infer (tags: gpu_id, quantized boolean, kv_cache_hit_count)
  - stream.emit (tags: emitted_tokens, first_token_ms)
- Sticky trace tags (must be propagated through every span): tenant_id, request_id, session_id, model_variant, route, pool_tier. These are used as join keys in the bento-box panels.
- Span-level error codes: use well-defined enum e.g., inference_timeout, model_oom, gradient_fallback, router_mismatch. Map these to alert groups.

Sampling rules for bento-box traces:
- Severity-weighted sampling (default): keep 100% of traces with errors or > p99 generation_tail_latency_ms; downsample warm success traces to 1%.
- Tenant-preserving rule: retain at least 5 traces/min per enterprise tenant while incident is ongoing.
- On-alert augmentation: temporarily raise sample rate to 100% for traces matching alert dimensions (route/model/pool).

Dashboard micro-panel layout (6 panels, left-to-right, top-to-bottom):
1) Top-line numbers: live TPS, p50/p90/p99 ttf_first_token_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate (single-row KPI).
2) Quantile heatmap: ttf_first_token_ms heatmap by tenant cohort (rows) vs sequence_length_bucket (cols). Color by p99.
3) Recent traces table: last 25 traces (timestamp, tenant_id, model_variant, error_code, quick-link to trace). Click to open full trace.
4) Binned tail latency: bar chart of generation_tail_latency_ms buckets with sample-count overlay.
5) Tenant contribution: stacked bar of top-10 tenants by request volume and corresponding p99 latency annotation.
6) Cost/efficiency mini: continuous_batching_efficiency trend + token_cost_ratio sparkline; annotate sudden cost spikes with autoscaler events.

Runbook sketch (90s triage -> 10m mitigation):
- 0–90s: glance KPIs (panel 1). If p99 or kv_cache_hit_rate degraded: jump to KV-check.
- KV-check (2–5m): open traces where kv.lookup.kv_hit==false; confirm if misses concentrated on particular tenant_shard or across pool. If tenant-specific ramp: throttle tenant or apply per-tenant routing to dedicated pool.
- Batch-check: if continuous_batching_efficiency drops, inspect batch.slot.batch_size distribution and recent autoscaler activity. If batch sizes shrunk due to front-end sampling or cookie, revert the config or increase burst capacity.
- Model fallback: check routing.resolve.fallback_reason; if fallback to larger model causing tail, rollback route policy.
- Quick mitigations (10m): enable temporary model-variant fallback to smaller model for affected route; enable kv-prefetch for top tenants; turn on circuit-breaker to drop long-running inferences (>Xs).

Alerting and thresholds (starter guide):
- P99 ttf_first_token_ms > 1200ms for 2 consecutive 1m buckets -> page SRE rotation.
- kv_cache_hit_rate drop > 15% absolute vs baseline for 5m -> page + notify product-owner channel.
- continuous_batching_efficiency drop > 25% vs rolling-1h -> notify infra and autoopen oncall checklist.
- quality regression: output_quality_regression_rate > 2x baseline for 24h -> page on-call and page ML research.

Dashboard UX notes (keep small & actionable):
- Avoid huge dashboard canvases. Each bento-box should fit a full laptop view without scrolling.
- Panel hover should show the join keys used (tenant_id, route, model_variant).
- Each trace in the recent-traces table must include a copy-button for trace-id and a one-click prompt-replay link for reproducing with the same prompt+model though sanitized.

Ownership & stewardship:
- Owner (primary): eng-observability (rotation lead: Miguel Torres).
- Backup owner: serving-runtime oncall.
- Quarterly review: checklist to validate metric derivations and thresholds (Confluence job).

Open questions and follow-ups (TODOs):
- Decide canonical token_cost_ratio ratecard and where finance sync lives (assigned: Emily Chen, due 2025-04-07).
- Add private-deploy annotation rules for airgapped traces (short note: send trace skeleton without PII).
- Prototype a CLI helper that given a trace-id prints the 90s triage summary (input: trace-id -> outputs: top 5 signal diffs). (owner: Arjun Patel).

Appendix: quick calculation examples
- Example ttf_first_token_ms for a sample trace: receive_time=10:01:00.100, first_token=10:01:00.720 -> ttf=620ms.
- Example kv_cache_hit_rate: kv_hits=4,800, kv_misses=200 over 5m -> hit_rate = 4800/(4800+200) = 96%

Notes on privacy & PII:
- Never store full prompt text in high-cardinality metrics. Store prompt-hash only and link to a sanitized replay system that strips PII. Enforce this in trace annotations: prompt_hash only.

Closing notes:
This is intentionally pragmatic and small. The bento-box is meant to be iterated quickly: prototyping in the telemetry sandbox, then moving to a more formal dashboard once oncall happy. Feedback welcome — ping #observability or drop comments on JIRA-OPS-4123.
